title: Protected night repositioning rounds and hospital-acquired pressure injuries on two medical wards
subtitle: QI project with PDSA cycles, stratified by night staffing
statement: Wards 7A and 7B recorded 41 hospital-acquired pressure injuries of category 2 or worse in a year, most found after night shifts, and on 46 percent of nights they ran with one registered nurse for more than seven patients. Night repositioning is the first task to slip. The project will test whether a protected night repositioning round with risk reassessment at the evening handover reduces pressure injuries, with results examined separately for poorly staffed nights.
whoAffected: Adult medical inpatients at high risk of pressure injury, especially older, immobile and acutely ill patients, and the night nurses and float nurses on wards 7A and 7B.
whatHurts: Pressure injuries cause pain, infection, longer stays and loss of dignity; nurses feel blamed for injuries that follow nights they could not staff safely.
currentPractice: Two-hourly repositioning is prescribed in the care plan but not protected; risk is scored at admission and weekly; a float nurse is sometimes available from the night bank.
whyNow: The board has asked for action and for evidence on staffing, the tissue viability team already inspects skin weekly, and the project is registered (QI-2026-054).
constraints: No additional nursing posts; any float nurse comes from the existing night bank. Changes must fit the electronic care plan without new build. Results are reported at ward level only, never by individual nurse.
patientCenteredGoal: No patient on wards 7A and 7B develops a pressure injury because a night was busy.
summary: Problem framed as a ward QI project on night repositioning, with staffing as a stratifier rather than the intervention.
